newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Japan insurer reaps forex rewards.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Japan insurer reaps forex rewards.

text.p: At a time when Japanese life insurance firms are struggling due to record-low domestic interest rates, Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd has avoided that pitfall by investing overseas and being aggressive in foreign exchange markets.
"In the past 1-1/2 years, our overseas investments have been successful," Masanori Mizoguchi, general manager of Nippon Dantai's securities investment department, told Reuters in an interview.
Currency dealers said Nippon Dantai, which sometimes buys and sells hundreds of millions of dollars a day, is one of the most active foreign exchange players in Tokyo.
"They have a major presence in the market," said one Tokyo currency dealer.
Mizoguchi said the ambitious moves had swollen the insurer's foreign currency-denominated assets to 900 billion yen, or about 22 percent of its total assets of four trillion yen.

The percentage is the highest among the 17 biggest Japanese life insurance firms, and is significantly more than the five percent or six percent figure for the nation's largest insurer, Nippon Life Insurance Co.
Nippon Dantai estimated that it had a return of more than 10 percent on its foreign investments last year, Mizoguchi said.

That is important because the industry is suffering due to record low interest rates paid on investments in Japan, and on April 25, the Finance Ministry ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to shut its business, the first failure of its kind in Japan's postwar history.
The collapse was partly due to the failure of investments in risky private placement offshore funds and because of the long-standing rock-bottom interest rates at home.
Analysts said other smaller insurers may be in similar trouble, but Nippon Dantai said it was in good shape.

"We have about 250 billion yen in undisclosed offshore assets, including unlisted Canadian bonds, but most of them have resulted in unrealised profits and we will disclose them in June," Mizoguchi said.

He said Nippon Dantai's strength was in its decision-making process in which managers of each investment section frequently discuss market developments and act promptly after deciding on the best investment tools.
Major insurers with a vertical decision-making structure are not as quick at making decisions and sometimes miss out on the best investment opportunities, analysts said.

But Mizoguchi said although he felt there were more risks in Japanese government bonds at the moment than in the foreign exchange market, he said Nippon Dantai was in no hurry to increase its foreign securities holdings since they were already at a high level.

He added that the firm's operations in the currency market were not aimed at reaping foreign exchange profits but at getting the best exchange rates for its new offshore investments and for its redemptions of such investments.
The company has about 200 billion yen worth of foreign bond holdings that will mature by the end of next March.
It plans to re-invest the money in foreign securities when the dollar falls below 125 yen, and may increase that by 100 billion to 200 billion if conditions allow, Mizoguchi said.
"The dollar may reach 130-135 yen by the end of this year and capital outflows may be accelerated after the revision of Foreign Exchange Control Law takes effect (in April 1998)," he added.
